identity: Opening chapter (الفصل الأول) of a modern Egyptian first-person confessional novel/memoir. A boy narrator — the family driver calls him أمين بك — is driven to his aunt Saadia's house, money-obsessed and resentful of his family's poverty, while the adults around him are visibly grieving over something he does not yet understand. The chapter interleaves four registers: interior monologue (paragraphs 1-4), scene narration introducing the driver صالح, the maid وصفية and the nurse دادة تفيدة (paragraphs 5-7), a short car dialogue rendered one speech turn per line (paragraphs 8-17), and a metafictional aside in which the narrator disclaims being an أديب and asks why and for whom he is writing at all (final paragraph), before snapping back to the aunt's rooftop. Register is literary MSA with light Egyptian colloquial inside the dialogue (أسطى، البيه، بكرة، طيب).
law: A sentence ends where a syntactically complete predication closes and the next token opens a NEW independent predication. The document itself proves that a leading connective does not block this: paragraphs — which are guaranteed sentence starts — open with فذهابي (177), ولكن (238), وقد (348), وتترك (494), فلماذا (509), وأمضي (545). So و/ف-initial main clauses that make a distinct assertion or discourse move are boundaries. STRONGEST signal is asyndeton: a fresh predication with no connective after a complete clause is always a boundary (كان 39, المهم 253, إن 265, أنا 275/280/592/652/764, لم تكن 405, لماذا 437, ماذا 487, هل 490, ما لي 553, كل شيء 569, أما 721, أحب 774, ملعب 780, لا يضايق 787). Also always a boundary: ولكن opening a rhetorical restart, and each member of an asyndetic question run. NOT a boundary: (a) anything opening with a backward-attaching subordinator — أن/أنني/الذي/التي/حين/كلما/إذا/حتى/بعد أن/ولو; (b) وإنما and بل correctives, which complete a single 'not X but Y' assertion rather than starting a new one; (c) وكأنما/كأنما comparative continuations, which are semantically subordinate; (d) coordinated members governed by one head (the أن-list at 122-137, the أو-alternatives at 690-705); (e) و-linked parallel clauses that jointly render ONE description or scene frame rather than advancing the argument. Mandatory and never removed: the 19 tokens immediately preceding an <NL> and the final token 792; an <NL> itself never carries a boundary.
reasoning: HARD SITE 1, the و-clause question. This is the whole document in miniature, and paragraph-initial ولكن/وقد/وتترك/وأمضي/فذهابي/فلماذا decide it: و is not a continuation guarantee here. But I refused to make it automatic, because that would shred the descriptive passages. The test I applied is whether the و-clause advances to a NEW assertion or merely adds a parallel member of one picture. Advancing, so marked: 50 (وأنا أذكر — pivot from the aunt's gifts to the narrator's own creed about money), 77 (وقد كنت — temporal jump 'from then until now'), 94 (وكنت لا أشعر — new grievance about Wagdi), 110 (ولم يكن يعنيني — opens the not-X-but-Y argument), 147 (وهو لا يكتفي — topic moves to the father's complaining), 599/607/616 (three successive وقد/وأنى moves in the literary argument), 679 (وقد يستحي), 757 (وعلى كل حال). Merely parallel, so NOT marked: 303 (كان السائق صالح يقود السيارة | وكانت معه الخادمة وصفية) and 383/393 (صالح صامت | ووصفية تشيح | وكلما ناديتها) — both are single comma-chained tableaux of who was in the car and what the mood was, and both are broken from outside by an asyndetic clause anyway (وقد ظلت at 348 is a new paragraph; لم تكن هذه الدموع تعنيني at 405 is asyndetic). Also declined: 258 (وهو دائما شعور مستقل — anaphoric expansion of 'ما أشعر به' itself, not a new claim) and 659 (وسواء عندي أصغى أو لم — tight coordinate rider on 'أحب الحديث'). | HARD SITE 2, وكأنما. Three occurrences at 163, 194 and 200, plus 390 and 412. I read كأنما as comparative and therefore backward-attaching, so none of them opens a sentence. The consequence is that paragraph 2 (177-212) has NO internal boundary at all: 'فذهابي إلى بيت عمتي سيعفيني... من هذا الفقر' plus its two وكأنما codas is one 36-token rhetorical sweep. I considered splitting at 193 and rejected it purely for consistency with 163, where the identical وكأنما construction closes paragraph 1. If the corpus treats كأنما as sentence-initial, 193 is my systematic miss and it costs me one boundary in that paragraph and nothing else. | HARD SITE 3, ف. This particle does two different jobs here and I split them. Inferential/meta ف, where the clause draws a conclusion about the whole preceding stretch, IS a boundary: 231 (فلا عجب إذن أن أفرح — إذن makes it explicitly a conclusion, and it closes out the argument running back through paragraph 2), 63 (فمعنى وجود القروش), 409 (فأنا أكلمهما), 415 (فقد كنت أنا سعيدا), 643 (ففيم إذن أكتب), 668 (فأنا شخصيا كإنسان), 728 (فإن القارئ). Narrative-sequence ف, where the clause is simply the next event in one causal chain, is NOT: I dropped 371 (فجاءت وصفية لتحمل عنها بعض العبء), because paragraph 6 is a single chain — Dada was alone, mother fell ill, Dada became unable, so Wasfiyya came — and the ف is its hinge, not a new sentence. This is the one place I knowingly treat two ف sites differently, and 231 vs 371 is the pair to grade me on. | HARD SITE 4, runs of questions. Asyndetic runs always split: 486/489 (لماذا ليس اليوم | ماذا جرى اليوم | هل هناك شيء) — three bare interrogatives with no connective, the clearest boundaries in the document. و-linked question pairs are judged by weight: split when each half is a substantial proposition or carries its own particle (246, where ولكن is repeated on both halves; 441, لماذا لا يتكلم الناس دائما | ولماذا يملون الاستماع إلي إذا استمر حديثي فترة طويلة), kept together when it is a short doublet on the same verb (589, لماذا أسوقه ولمن أسوقه — two tokens each, one rhetorical breath; and 646, ففيم إذن أكتب ومن تراه قارئ ما أكتب). | HARD SITE 5, index 587 vs 584. 'أنا لا أدري لماذا أكتب هذا الكلام هذا الحديث جميعا لماذا أسوقه'. Two parses: (a) 'هذا الحديث جميعا' is an appositive to 'هذا الكلام', closing the sentence at 587; (b) it is a fronted topic of 'لماذا أسوقه', closing the previous sentence at 584. I chose (a) — the appositive re-naming reads more naturally and (b) would leave 'لماذا أكتب هذا الكلام' oddly clipped — but I hold it only at med, and 584 is the alternative if I am wrong. | HARD SITE 6, the narration/speech seam at 494-507. 'وتترك وصفية دموعها ونظرها إلى الطريق وتسارع بالإجابة | لا أبدا | وماذا يمكن أن يحدث'. The frame verbs وتترك/وتسارع share a subject and stay joined. 501 is the colon site where narration hands over to quoted speech; I mark it lo because conventions differ on whether a colon terminates. 503 I mark med: 'لا أبدا' is a complete denial and 'وماذا يمكن أن يحدث' is a separate question. Same logic gives 513 (أنا أبدا | أنا لا أبكي) and 519 (كذا ربما | ولماذا لا تعلمني أنت السواقة). I declined the tempting one-word splits at 512 (أنا) and 518 (كذا) — plausible as incredulous echoes, but too thin to bet on. | HARD SITE 7, index 746. 'ولكن من يدري لعل هذا الكتاب يجد من يصوغه'. 'من يدري' is a fixed rhetorical question and لعل naturally opens a fresh clause, but the two also read as one comma-joined thought. Genuine coin flip, marked lo. | HARD SITE 8, the closing snap-back. After the metafictional passage, 774 (أحب من بيت عمتي سطح البيت) is asyndetic AND a hard topic jump back into the narrative — a certain boundary. Then 779 and 786 are the softer question of whether 'ملعب واسع ألعب فيه الكرة مع وجدي' and 'لا يضايق لعبنا أحد أو سيارة' are appositive commas or full stops; both are asyndetic, which is my strongest signal, so I marked them at med rather than hi to register that appositive-comma remains live. | DENSITY CHECK. 76 sentences over 773 non-<NL> tokens, about 10 tokens each. That average is pulled down by the dialogue, where turns are genuinely 3-5 tokens. The narrative paragraph 1 comes out at 17 tokens per sentence and the choppy metafictional paragraph at about 9, which matches the audible change in register — the narrator's self-interrogation really does run in short bursts. I take that spread as evidence the granularity is calibrated rather than uniform-and-arbitrary.
